details: For T>=1, endpoint-complete threshold chains give $\mathrm L\ge\lfloor\log_2(\mathrm T+1)\rfloor$, hence $\mathrm L\ge(1/2)\log_2\mathrm T$. Logarithms apply to positive T only.
proof: An endpoint-complete threshold witness of dimension T supplies T+1 ordered traces. Balanced binary search using the witnessing coordinates shatters a tree of depth floor(log_2(T+1)). This is at least floor(log_2 T), hence at least (1/2)log_2 T for positive integer T. At T=0 the logarithmic expression is not used.
name: Littlestone Dimension / Threshold Dimension (logarithmic)
proof_source: LaTeX survey, Lemma lem:endpoint-threshold-littlestone; direct binary-search proof in the endpoint convention.
